## Multiple Response Frequencies

### Load Libraries
```{r}
library(knitr)
library(rmarkdown)
library(htmlTable)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readxl)
```

### Load Data
```{r}
setwd("~/Desktop/projects/r-starter")
# Replace 'your_dataset.csv' with the actual dataset file name
df <- read_xlsx("./MR_Drugs.xlsx")  # Ensure the dataset is in the working directory
df
```

### Process Multiple Response Data
```{r}
# Define multiple response columns
income_mr_cols <- c("inco1", "inco2", "inco3", "inco4", "inco5", "inco6", "inco7")

# Convert wide format to long format
income_long <- df %>%
  select(all_of(income_mr_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Income_MR", values_to = "Response") %>%
  filter(Response == 1)  # Keep only selected responses

# Compute frequencies
income_freq <- income_long %>%
  group_by(Income_MR) %>%
  summarise(N = n()) %>%
  mutate(Percent = round((N / sum(N)) * 100, 1))

# Count unique cases
total_cases <- n_distinct(df$id)  # Ensure there is a unique respondent ID column

# Compute percent of cases
income_freq <- income_freq %>%
  mutate(Percent_Cases = round((N / total_cases) * 100, 1))

# Add Total row
income_freq <- income_freq %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(
    Income_MR = "Total",
    N = sum(income_freq$N),
    Percent = 100.0,
    Percent_Cases = round(sum(income_freq$Percent_Cases), 1)
  ))
```

### Display Frequency Table with htmlTable
```{r}
htmlTable(
  income_freq,
  rnames = FALSE,  # Hide row names
  header = c("", "N", "Percent", "Percent_Cases"),  # Correct column names
  cgroup = c("", "Responses", ""),  # Group headers
  n.cgroup = c(1, 2, 1),  # Specify how many columns each header spans
  align = "lccc",  # Align text in columns
  css.table = "margin: 20px; padding: 10px; color: black; border: 1px solid black; width: 50%;",  # Add margin and padding to the table element
  css.cell = "padding: 15px;"  # Add padding to each cell
)
```

## Multiple Response Analysis
```{r}
library(foreign)
setwd("/Users/admin/Desktop/projects/r-starter")
# Create the data for the second table: "My friends will think I'm stupid for not being able to cope with SPSS"
friends_spss <- read.spss("./Mandip\ -\ SAQ8.sav", to.data.frame = TRUE)

# Combine all responses into a single vector
all_responses <- unlist(friends_spss)

# Get unique values and their frequencies
unique_values <- unique(all_responses)
frequency <- table(all_responses)

# Calculate total number of responses
total_responses <- length(all_responses)

# Calculate percentage
percent <- round((frequency / total_responses) * 100, 1)

# Valid percent is the same as percent in this case (no missing values assumed)
valid_percent <- percent

# Calculate cumulative percent
cumulative_percent <- round(cumsum(percent), 1)

# Create the result data frame
result_table <- data.frame(
  Valid = names(frequency),
  Frequency = as.numeric(frequency),
  Percent = as.numeric(percent),
  "Valid Percent" = as.numeric(valid_percent),
  "Cumulative Percent" = as.numeric(cumulative_percent)
)

# Add a "Total" row
total_row <- data.frame(
  Valid = "Total",
  Frequency = total_responses,
  Percent = 100.0,
  "Valid Percent" = 100.0,
  "Cumulative Percent" = 100.0
)

# Combine the result table and the total row
final_result <- rbind(result_table, total_row)

# Generate HTML for the second table
htmlTable(
  final_result,
  caption = "My friends will think I'm stupid for not being able to cope with SPSS",
  rnames = FALSE,
  align = "lccc",  # Align text in columns
  css.table = "margin: 20px; padding: 10px; color: black; border: 1px solid black; width:100%;",  # Add margin and padding to the table element
  css.cell = "padding: 15px;border: 1px solid black;" , # Add padding to each cell  align = "lccc",  # Align text in columns
  cell.header = "padding: 15px;"  # Add padding to each cell
)
```
